sources.title: National Park Service, National Survey of Historic Sites and Buildings: New York City Hall (1959; NRHP 66000539)

lengthM.note: length (P2043, 215.75 ft): the front from wing end to wing end

storeys.note: number of floors above ground (P1101): two storeys over a raised basement

heightM.note: the cupola's tip above the street, proportioned by eye (no PD/CC0 figure found); a plain needle stands in for the statue (LEGAL-1: no figures)

wallM.note: the main cornice above the street: a raised basement and two tall storeys

basementM.note: the raised basement storey, drawn as a darker rusticated band

roofM.note: the low hipped roof behind the balustrade

centreBlock.note: the front length less the two wings; the depth is an estimate

wing.note: each end wing's width (two bays) and how far it projects ahead of the centre block (the C-shaped plan the NPS survey's engravings show)

portico.note: the central columned portico at the main storey, with a balustrade over it

porticoM.note: the portico's top above the street

stepsM.note: how far the broad front steps run out ahead of the portico

cupolaBaseWidthM.note: the cupola's square lower stage across (the clock stage, drawn plain: no dial or text)

cupolaDomeM.note: the dome's rise over the drum

lanternM.note: the small lantern on the dome

readabilityScale.note: No thin members: columns are drawn at their real proportion to the bay, windows as punched glass quads.

gameScale.note: Game scale (orchestrator decision 2026-10-08, the user may overrule): heights x1.8 so the hall and its cupola read at the 3,000-4,500 m game camera; the plan x1.25, the most that fits the frame's exclusion (86 x 60 m).
